solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post, which drops the counts, so each count is read off the blogger's answer

clue.text: Ruler's still virtually one foot

indicators.note: virtually means nearly but not quite, so the word for still loses its final letter

parts.note: still as in calm, without wind
the Roman numeral for one
F is the abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: A monarch who is still, practically speaking, a single foot tall.
explanation.walkthrough: CALIF is a variant spelling of caliph.
explanation.definitionFit: A calif, or caliph, was the civil and religious head of a Muslim state, so a ruler.

clue.text: Dispatching one, skipper will receive special help for handling cables

indicators.note: receiving means taking something inside, so the skipper's word holds the abbreviation within it
dispatching means sending away, so one letter is removed from the skipper's word

parts.note: a skipper is the captain of a ship or team
the Roman numeral for one, which is removed
S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: A ship's master, sending one sailor away, is given extra help with the mooring ropes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatching one' removes the Roman numeral from the skipper word before the special letter is slipped inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is the upright revolving drum on a ship used to wind in heavy ropes and anchor chains.

clue.text: PM is more behind exploiting notion it turned out

indicators.note: turned out means expelled, so the two letters spelling it are thrown out of the word notion

parts.note: the comparative of aft, a sailor's word for behind
taken as written
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister lagging further behind because of an idea that proved mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister but is the time of day. Taking I and T out of NOTION leaves NOON.
explanation.definitionFit: PM, post meridiem, denotes the hours after midday, which is the afternoon.

clue.text: Locksmith does this on getting into restraints

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so the short word goes inside the word for restraints

parts.note: lids as in things that keep a lid on, i.e. restraints
o' is a short form of on, as in Chambers

explanation.surface: A locksmith's job described as clamping on handcuffs.
explanation.walkthrough: To loid is slang for slipping a lock with a strip of celluloid, a trick a locksmith (or burglar) may use.
explanation.definitionFit: Loid, short for celluloid, is a verb meaning to open a spring lock with a plastic strip, which locksmiths do.

clue.text: It's about fluid with a nose mostly

definitions.text: It's about fluid with a nose mostly

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the slang word for nose drops its last letter

parts.note: FL is the abbreviation for fluid
taken as written
conk is slang for nose

explanation.surface: A description of a perfume bottle: all about the liquid and the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a flacon surrounds fluid, and perfume is all about the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A flacon is a small stoppered scent bottle, a container wrapped around liquid destined for the nose.

clue.text: More up for it here in Hamburg taking in old service

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so the German word holds the other letters

parts.note: hier is German for here, as said in Hamburg
O is the abbreviation for old
the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Someone in Hamburg grows keener after attending an old church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Horny is slang for sexually aroused, so the comparative means more keen for sex.

clue.text: Clues of that bloke including those bordering on naughtiest

indicators.note: including means holding inside, so the possessive surrounds the selected letters

parts.note: belonging to him

indicators.note: bordering means at the edges, so only the outside letters of the following word are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of naughtiest

explanation.surface: A man's tips that verge on the very cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Hints are suggestions or pointers towards a solution, just as clues are.

clue.text: Editor pressed by mates made an objection

parts.note: oppos is slang for mates or colleagues
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor, leaned on by friends, raised a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the editor sits under, so is pressed by, the mates; oppo is British slang for a partner or pal.
explanation.definitionFit: To have opposed something is to have spoken against it, that is to have objected.

clue.text: Reform meant take off ID?

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the next word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
to take off someone is to mimic or ape them

explanation.surface: Changed intent: remove your identity card?
explanation.walkthrough: A nametape is a strip of tape sewn into clothing, such as a school uniform, bearing its owner's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A nametape is a cloth label identifying a garment's owner, a form of identification, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Old bumpkin in hostels no longer supplying loads

indicators.note: in places one item within another, so the bumpkin is put inside the hostels word

parts.note: in is an obsolete spelling of inn, so a word for hostels no longer used
put is an obsolete word for a rustic or yokel

explanation.surface: A yokel of old staying in youth hostels that no longer exist, carrying heavy loads.
explanation.definitionFit: To input data is to feed or load it into a computer, so inputs means loads in that sense.

clue.text: Angry person holds in grouse

indicators.note: holds in means contains, so the answer sits inside the words before it

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A furious person keeps their complaints bottled up.
explanation.walkthrough: Grouse looks like a verb meaning complain; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Ryper is the plural of rype, a Scandinavian name for the ptarmigan, which is a grouse.

clue.text: Whim to embrace cheek before Pastor's light-heartedness

indicators.note: embracing means hugging something within, so the word for whim wraps round the rest

parts.note: a fancy is a whim
lip is impudence, cheek
P is an abbreviation for pastor

explanation.surface: A sudden urge to kiss a vicar on the cheek, all very light-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply places the cheek word ahead of the pastor's letter inside the whim.
explanation.definitionFit: Flippancy is an unserious, frivolous attitude, a kind of disrespectful light-heartedness.

clue.text: It is in pot making tea of sorts

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a pan is a cooking pot
'tis is the contraction of it is

explanation.surface: Something placed in a teapot to brew a kind of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A ptisan, or tisane, is a herbal infusion, a type of tea.

clue.text: Increase strength in the morning with shaver (5, two words)

parts.note: am, ante meridiem, is before noon
a young shaver is a youngster; pup is a cheeky young lad

explanation.surface: Boosting one's power first thing with an electric razor.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaver suggests a razor, but a young shaver is a boy, and pup is a cheeky youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: To amp up is an informal phrase meaning to intensify or boost, raising the strength of something.

clue.text: Dutch is in part an old charmer

indicators.note: is in places the abbreviation inside the next word

parts.note: a sector is a part or section
Du. is the abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: A Dutchman playing a role as an ageing smooth-talker.
explanation.definitionFit: Seductor is an archaic word for a seducer, someone who charms and leads others astray.

clue.text: In Cannes I cannot concentrate lifting honour in cut marble (9, two words)

indicators.note: in places the raised honour word inside the trimmed marble word
cut means trimmed, so the marble word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tolley is a large shooting marble

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue means raising up, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to fete someone is to honour them

explanation.surface: A French visitor to Cannes admits to being unable to focus on lifting a medal from a marble block.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cannes signals a French phrase: tête folle, literally mad head.
explanation.definitionFit: Tête folle is French for a scatterbrain, someone whose head is all over the place and cannot concentrate.

clue.text: Accursed chap on abridged Chambers, say

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the general word that Chambers exemplifies is cut down

parts.note: a chap is a male
Chambers is a well-known dictionary, an example of one

explanation.surface: A man cursing a shortened edition of the crossword setter's favourite reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: Dict is the usual short form of dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Maledict is an archaic adjective meaning cursed, from Latin male dictus, spoken ill of.

clue.text: I'll stand for last of these in compiler that's hard to get wrong

indicators.note: standing for something means taking its place, so the letter I replaces another inside the compiler word

parts.note: a crossword compiler is a setter

indicators.note: last of picks out only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: final letter of these, which is swapped out
taken as written, the replacement letter

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of a clue so simple no solver could miss it.
explanation.walkthrough: SETTER has I put in place of an E, giving SITTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitter is an easy chance, like a sitting target, something one could hardly fail at.

clue.text: Before noon poet is moving with moderate pace

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ante, Latin for before
N is the abbreviation for noon
Dante Alighieri, the Italian poet

explanation.surface: Ahead of midday a poet sets off at an unhurried walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before noon' wants to be AM; split it, so 'Before' gives A and 'noon' gives N.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a musical direction meaning at a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: Bullish? Go sticking in gold

indicators.note: sticking in means lodged inside, so the gold symbol goes inside the word for go

parts.note: trine is an obsolete verb meaning to go
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A stock-market query: is the market rising? Then put money into gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Bullish looks like stock-market jargon for optimism; it is meant literally, like a bull.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurine means relating to or resembling a bull, from Latin taurus.

clue.text: Annals of Tacitus or Ovid's poem? Sound bit of instruction

definitions.text: Annals of Tacitus or Ovid's poem

parts.note: fast as in sound asleep, firm and secure

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here just its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of instruction

explanation.surface: A classics student asking whether the reference is to Tacitus's histories or Ovid's verse, and getting good advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Fasti were Roman calendars and chronological registers, the word Tacitus used for annals, and Ovid's poem on the Roman year is titled Fasti.

clue.text: Resolution of mostly regional division amongst archaeologists (7, two words)

indicators.note: a resolution breaks something down and settles it anew, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the next word goes

parts.note: taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: Settling a dispute over local boundaries among a team of excavators.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Age is one of the periods into which archaeologists divide prehistory, after the Bronze Age.

clue.text: Bits of fibre and, informally, juices?

parts.note: 'n' is the casual form of and, as in rock 'n' roll
juice is informal for fuel, so oils are a kind of juice

explanation.surface: Fragments of fibre in fruit juices, put casually.
explanation.definitionFit: Noils are the short fibres combed out of wool or silk before spinning, small pieces of fibre.

clue.text: One for L'Académie française in Italian's online store

indicators.note: in places the French word inside the Italian possessive

parts.note: It. is the abbreviation for Italian, plus the 's
une is French for one, as the French Academy would have it

explanation.surface: A French language academy member shopping for something Italian on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: iTunes is Apple's digital media shop on the internet, selling music and video.

clue.text: Fitter on trailer modifying attachment

parts.note: a trailer for a film is an advertisement, an ad
more fit or suitable, more apt

explanation.surface: A mechanic attaching something to a trailer to modify it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitter' looks like a mechanic and the definition; it means more apt, and goes after, or on, the trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: An adapter is a fitting that lets one device connect to another, an accessory that modifies a connection.

clue.text: Insight shown by a group of Christian fellows

parts.note: taken as written
a Christian Union, a student Christian society
fellows are men

explanation.surface: Wisdom displayed by members of a church fellowship.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is keen judgement and perception, sharp insight into situations.

clue.text: You see this up in Canada — function with Evian, eg

definitions.text: You see this up in Canada

parts.note: cot is the short form of cotangent, a trigonometric function
Evian is a brand of mineral water, eau in French

explanation.surface: A Canadian event where a function serves bottled water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is literal: the thing is raised ground.
explanation.definitionFit: In Canada a coteau is a ridge or tract of high land, something seen rising up.

clue.text: Horace's in the presence of Owen initially in the old lie

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the word for the old lie

parts.note: cram is old slang for a lie

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the name is used

parts.note: first letter of Owen

explanation.surface: Echoing Wilfred Owen's poem calling the Horatian maxim, it is sweet to die for one's country, the old lie.
explanation.walkthrough: Owen's war poem Dulce et Decorum Est calls Horace's line about dying for one's country 'the old Lie'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coram is the Latin preposition meaning in the presence of, as Horace would have written it.

clue.text: Migrant with spare brass appearing in street

parts.note: first meaning: a small migratory sandpiper
second meaning: to be sparing, to restrict

indicators.note: appearing in means showing up inside, so the money word goes inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
brass and tin are both slang for money

explanation.surface: A newcomer with spare cash turning up on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass is northern British slang for money, as is tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A stint is a small wading bird that migrates, and to stint is to spare or use frugally.

clue.text: Sound catty without direct upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: w/o is the abbreviation for without
to direct is to aim

explanation.surface: Someone sounding spiteful without being openly hostile.
explanation.walkthrough: Catty suggests spiteful; here it means literally like a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: To miaow is to make the cry of a cat, so to sound like a cat.

clue.text: Model in to run a lottery in Perth, perhaps (8, two words)

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the following letters are moulded into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fashion model entering a raffle in Western Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth here is the city in Western Australia, not the Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia and New Zealand an art union is a lottery, originally one with artworks as prizes.

clue.text: Newton in undoing argument

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for undoing

parts.note: one's undoing is one's ruin
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: Isaac Newton disproving a theory.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is an informal word for a quarrel or confrontation, an argument.

clue.text: Emperor accepted in Tuileries Palace, the prodigious bounder

parts.note: Imp. is the abbreviation for emperor, Latin imperator
A is the abbreviation for accepted
la is French for the, as used in the Paris palace

explanation.surface: Napoleon received in the Tuileries Palace, an extraordinary cad.
explanation.walkthrough: Bounder suggests a cad, but here it is an animal that leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope famous for its enormous leaps, so a prodigious jumper.

clue.text: Smart chap eg expert about northern officer checking wallop

parts.note: a smart alec is a know-all

indicators.note: about means around, so the expert word surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: a oner is an expert, someone unique at something
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A clever specialist from the north inspecting a heavy blow.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallop is British slang for beer, not just a hard hit.
explanation.definitionFit: An ale conner was a medieval borough official who tested the quality of ale, the beer called wallop.

clue.text: Mittens adjusted appropriately for fine snare (7, two words)

indicators.note: adjusted means altered and set right, so the letters are rearranged to fit

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Gloves altered to suit the needs of a trapper.
explanation.definitionFit: A mist net is a very fine mesh net used by ornithologists to trap birds, a delicate snare.

clue.text: No good and tiny bit of African rhino

parts.note: NG is the abbreviation for no good
wee means tiny

explanation.surface: A small, useless piece of an African rhinoceros.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhino is old British slang for money, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The ngwee is a small coin of Zambia, a hundredth of a kwacha, so a bit of African money.
